verdict: Microsoft Project: Choose Microsoft Project/Planner when Microsoft 365 is the system of work and traditional scheduling/portfolio depth matters — landscape on modern Work OS lists. Scores use the project-management editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Not a modern Work OS peer
bestFor: Enterprise portfolio planning on higher plans
notIdealFor: Startups wanting modern Work OS UX
tradeoffs: Seat minimums and AI credit bundles vs published per-seat floors
Work OS breadth vs specialist timeline / PDF / remote / desktop depth
Automation and reporting depth vs ease of use for small teams
Included AI credits vs paid AI add-ons or credit top-ups
recommendation: Choose Microsoft Project/Planner when Microsoft 365 is the system of work and traditional scheduling/portfolio depth matters — landscape on modern Work OS lists. Compare Smartsheet for spreadsheet PMO, monday/Asana for modern Work OS, and Jira for engineering delivery.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Familiar inside M365 but classic Project scheduling has a learning curve vs Asana.
Gantt, dependencies and resource scheduling are a traditional PM strength — 9.
Power Automate helps; native PM automation thinner than ClickUp/monday.
Teams/M365 collaboration is strong when the org is already there.
Deepest Microsoft ecosystem story in this category set — 9.
Solid project/portfolio reporting on higher plans.
Enterprise PMO scale path via Plan 3/5.
Plan 3/5 seats are premium vs modern Work OS floors; value depends on M365 standardisation. Affiliate economics excluded.
Copilot-adjacent AI may apply via M365 — not Motion-class product AI.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine project-management editorial criteria using the category weights (work planning 15, automation & workflows 14, ease of use 12, collaboration 12, integrations 12, reporting 10, value 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — work OS / PM peers, timeline specialists, and adjacent PDF / remote-access / desktop-workspace tools are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
